subject: MSA + Order Form: derivative/feedback carveouts and training consent path

Subject: MSA + Order Form: IP & training carveouts — initial questions

Mina,

Thanks for the intro earlier. Parity's legal team ran through the MSA and Order Form draft and flagged three items that need alignment before procurement will clear the PO: output ownership for generated clinical content, explicit opt-out for model training/retention, and whether feedback we provide can be used for general model improvement.

High-level asks from our side:
- Parity requires that any clinical outputs tied to our protected templates are not assigned to Redwood for productization without explicit consent.
- We need a training opt-out option for certain data classes (PHI/identified templates) with confirmation that data will be excluded from any training sets.
- Feedback submitted through support channels should have an opt-in toggle for sharing back to vendor training pipelines (we can provide examples).

Attached is a short list of questions and examples (Parity_Initial_Questions.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood's standard place to land on these and whether you have recommended contract language or a tradeoff path? We are on a tight procurement timeline — ideally finalize legal language by EOW next week.

Elena Russo

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal quick sync with legal + product (I will schedule for tomorrow).
2) We’ll produce two alternative redline approaches: (A) narrow carveouts + telemetry retention for reliability, (B) broader opt-out that includes explicit non-productization language but with higher support/ops constraints.
3) Share candidate clauses by EOD Wed so you have time to review before procurement runs the PO next Friday.

Can you confirm the latest acceptable signing date and whether Parity prefers order-form-level carveouts or a standalone exhibit? Also attaching a short internal note (Redwood_MSATransition_issues.docx) that captures initial gaps.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Draft redlines — training, output, feedback (for Mina to send)

Mina — following our sync, attached below are proposed drafting options and rationale. This is intended for Mina to edit/send to Parity as our starting position. Key tradeoffs are highlighted.

Option 1 (operationally light; narrow carveout):
- Output: Customer retains exclusive rights to outputs that reproduce or are substantially similar to Customer-provided template content. For derivative productization purposes, Redwood retains a non-exclusive license to aggregated, non-identifying outputs for internal model diagnostics.
- Training: Customer may designate data classes for exclusion from training (e.g., templates labeled PHI). Exclusion is implemented via our data ingress filters; Redwood will not include excluded items in training datasets used for public model updates.
- Feedback: Feedback submitted via support or optional telemetry may be used in de-identified aggregate form for model improvements; Customer may opt-out of such sharing via an Order Form flag.

Option 2 (customer-protective; higher ops cost):
- Output: Customer retains exclusive ownership of outputs and can require Redwood to execute an assignment for any outputs that Customer asserts are productized. Redwood may request evidence and reserve a review period.
- Training: All customer datasets and outputs are excluded from vendor model training unless Customer provides explicit written permission.
- Feedback: Any feedback that contains Customer Confidential Information will be treated as Customer Confidential and not used for vendor training; Redwood will provide a fast-track review and redaction option.

Implementation notes:
- Telemetry/diagnostics: we should preserve a minimal telemetry channel (error rates, latency, anonymized prompt histograms) to investigate regressions; seek carveout that allows those signals without token-level retention.
- Evidence and dispute path: propose a 30-day meet-and-confer with engineering to resolve disputed productization claims before any assignment requirement.

Ben — flag anything operationally infeasible. Mina — once you approve I will convert to redline markup.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Legal (inference)
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Mina — thanks for the quick turnaround and please thank Karthik and Ben for the options. Parity prefers Option 2 (customer-protective) for core clinical templates; we can accept Option 1 for non-clinical telemetry. Two asks before we sign:

1) Please incorporate the Option 2 language as redline in the attached Order Form (Parity_OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx).
2) Can Redwood commit to the 30-day meet-and-confer and provide a single point of contact in engineering for evidence review?

We are comfortable with the proposed DocuSign cadence once legal language is finalized. I attached our annotated order form. If you can send an updated redline by EOD Thu we will route internally for final signoff.
